lines.text: Like a true friar. Moe reasons for this action

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: At our more leisure shall I render you;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Only, this one: Lord Angelo is precise;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Stands at a guard with envy; scarce confesses

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That his blood flows or that his appetite

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Is more to bread than stone. Hence shall we see,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: If power change purpose, what our seemers be.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Isabella and Francisca, a Nun.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And have you nuns no farther privileges?

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: Are not these large enough?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Yes, truly; I speak not as desiring more,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: But rather wishing a more strict restraint

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Upon the sisterhood, the votarists of Saint Clare.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Ho! Peace be in this place!

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Who’s that which calls?

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: It is a man’s voice. Gentle Isabella,

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: Turn you the key, and know his business of him;

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: You may, I may not; you are yet unsworn.

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: When you have vowed, you must not speak with men

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: But in the presence of the prioress;

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: Then, if you speak, you must not show your face;

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: Or if you show your face, you must not speak.

lines.speaker: FRANCISCA
lines.text: He calls again. I pray you answer him.
[_Exit Francisca._]

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Peace and prosperity! Who is’t that calls?
Enter Lucio.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Hail, virgin, if you be, as those cheek-roses

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Proclaim you are no less. Can you so stead me

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: As bring me to the sight of Isabella,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: A novice of this place, and the fair sister

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: To her unhappy brother Claudio?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Why “her unhappy brother”? let me ask,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: The rather for I now must make you know

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I am that Isabella, and his sister.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Gentle and fair, your brother kindly greets you.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Not to be weary with you, he’s in prison.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Woe me! For what?

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: For that which, if myself might be his judge,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: He should receive his punishment in thanks:

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: He hath got his friend with child.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Sir, make me not your story.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: ’Tis true.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: I would not, though ’tis my familiar sin

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: With maids to seem the lapwing, and to jest,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Tongue far from heart, play with all virgins so.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: I hold you as a thing enskied and sainted

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: By your renouncement an immortal spirit,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: And to be talked with in sincerity,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: As with a saint.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: You do blaspheme the good in mocking me.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Do not believe it. Fewness and truth, ’tis thus:

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Your brother and his lover have embraced;

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: As those that feed grow full, as blossoming time

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: That from the seedness the bare fallow brings

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: To teeming foison, even so her plenteous womb

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Expresseth his full tilth and husbandry.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Someone with child by him? My cousin Juliet?

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Is she your cousin?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Adoptedly, as school-maids change their names

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: By vain though apt affection.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: She it is.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: O, let him marry her!

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: This is the point.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: The Duke is very strangely gone from hence;

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Bore many gentlemen, myself being one,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: In hand, and hope of action; but we do learn,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: By those that know the very nerves of state,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: His givings-out were of an infinite distance

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: From his true-meant design. Upon his place,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: And with full line of his authority,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Governs Lord Angelo; a man whose blood

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Is very snow-broth; one who never feels

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: The wanton stings and motions of the sense;

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: But doth rebate and blunt his natural edge

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: With profits of the mind, study and fast.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: He, to give fear to use and liberty,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Which have for long run by the hideous law

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: As mice by lions, hath picked out an act,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Under whose heavy sense your brother’s life

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Falls into forfeit. He arrests him on it,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: And follows close the rigour of the statute

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: To make him an example. All hope is gone,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Unless you have the grace by your fair prayer

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: To soften Angelo. And that’s my pith of business

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: ’Twixt you and your poor brother.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Doth he so

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Seek his life?

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Has censured him already;

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: And, as I hear, the Provost hath a warrant

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: For’s execution.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Alas, what poor ability’s in me

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To do him good?

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Assay the power you have.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: My power? Alas, I doubt.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Our doubts are traitors,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: And make us lose the good we oft might win

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: By fearing to attempt. Go to Lord Angelo,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: And let him learn to know, when maidens sue,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: Men give like gods; but when they weep and kneel,

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: All their petitions are as freely theirs

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: As they themselves would owe them.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I’ll see what I can do.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: But speedily.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I will about it straight;

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: No longer staying but to give the Mother

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Notice of my affair. I humbly thank you.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Commend me to my brother. Soon at night

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I’ll send him certain word of my success.

lines.speaker: LUCIO
lines.text: I take my leave of you.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Good sir, adieu.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Angelo, Escalus, Servants, and a Justice.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: We must not make a scarecrow of the law,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Setting it up to fear the birds of prey,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And let it keep one shape till custom make it

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Their perch, and not their terror.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Ay, but yet

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Let us be keen, and rather cut a little

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Than fall and bruise to death. Alas, this gentleman,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Whom I would save, had a most noble father.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Let but your honour know,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Whom I believe to be most strait in virtue,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: That, in the working of your own affections,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Had time cohered with place, or place with wishing,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Or that the resolute acting of your blood

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Could have attained th’ effect of your own purpose,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Whether you had not sometime in your life

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Erred in this point which now you censure him,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: And pulled the law upon you.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: ’Tis one thing to be tempted, Escalus,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Another thing to fall. I not deny

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: The jury passing on the prisoner’s life

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: May in the sworn twelve have a thief or two

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Guiltier than him they try. What’s open made to justice,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That justice seizes. What knows the laws

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That thieves do pass on thieves? ’Tis very pregnant,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: The jewel that we find, we stoop and take ’t,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Because we see it; but what we do not see,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: We tread upon, and never think of it.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: You may not so extenuate his offence

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: For I have had such faults; but rather tell me,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: When I that censure him do so offend,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Let mine own judgement pattern out my death,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And nothing come in partial. Sir, he must die.
Enter Provost.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Be it as your wisdom will.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Where is the Provost?

lines.speaker: PROVOST
lines.text: Here, if it like your honour.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: See that Claudio

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Be executed by nine tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Bring him his confessor, let him be prepared,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: For that’s the utmost of his pilgrimage.
[_Exit Provost._]

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Well, heaven forgive him; and forgive us all.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Some rise by sin, and some by virtue fall.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Some run from brakes of vice, and answer none,

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: And some condemned for a fault alone.
Enter Elbow and Officers with Froth and Pompey.

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Come, bring them away. If these be good people in a commonweal that do

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: nothing but use their abuses in common houses, I know no law. Bring

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: them away.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: How now, sir, what’s your name? And what’s the matter?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: If it please your honour, I am the poor Duke’s constable, and my name

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: is Elbow. I do lean upon justice, sir, and do bring in here before your

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: good honour two notorious benefactors.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Benefactors? Well, what benefactors are they? Are they not malefactors?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: If it please your honour, I know not well what they are, but precise

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: villains they are, that I am sure of, and void of all profanation in

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: the world that good Christians ought to have.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: This comes off well. Here’s a wise officer.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Go to. What quality are they of? Elbow is your name? Why dost thou not

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: speak, Elbow?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: He cannot, sir. He’s out at elbow.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: What are you, sir?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: He, sir? A tapster, sir; parcel bawd; one that serves a bad woman;

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: whose house, sir, was, as they say, plucked down in the suburbs; and

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: now she professes a hot-house, which, I think is a very ill house too.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: How know you that?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: My wife, sir, whom I detest before heaven and your honour—

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: How? Thy wife?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Ay, sir, whom I thank heaven is an honest woman—

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Dost thou detest her therefore?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: I say, sir, I will detest myself also, as well as she, that this house,

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: if it be not a bawd’s house, it is pity of her life, for it is a

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: naughty house.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: How dost thou know that, constable?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Marry, sir, by my wife, who, if she had been a woman cardinally given,

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: might have been accused in fornication, adultery, and all uncleanliness

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: there.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: By the woman’s means?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Ay, sir, by Mistress Overdone’s means; but as she spit in his face, so

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: she defied him.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Sir, if it please your honour, this is not so.

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Prove it before these varlets here, thou honourable man, prove it.
[_To Angelo_.]

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Do you hear how he misplaces?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Sir, she came in great with child; and longing, saving your honour’s

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: reverence, for stewed prunes; sir, we had but two in the house, which

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: at that very distant time stood, as it were, in a fruit dish, a dish of

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: some threepence; your honours have seen such dishes; they are not china

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: dishes, but very good dishes—

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Go to, go to. No matter for the dish, sir.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: No, indeed, sir, not of a pin; you are therein in the right. But to the

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: point. As I say, this Mistress Elbow, being, as I say, with child, and

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: being great-bellied, and longing, as I said, for prunes; and having but

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: two in the dish, as I said, Master Froth here, this very man, having

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: eaten the rest, as I said, and, as I say, paying for them very

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: honestly; for, as you know, Master Froth, I could not give you

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: threepence again—

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: No, indeed.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Very well. You being then, if you be remembered, cracking the stones of

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: the foresaid prunes—

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: Ay, so I did indeed.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Why, very well. I telling you then, if you be remembered, that such a

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: one and such a one were past cure of the thing you wot of, unless they

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: kept very good diet, as I told you—

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: All this is true.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Why, very well then—

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Come, you are a tedious fool. To the purpose. What was done to Elbow’s

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: wife that he hath cause to complain of? Come me to what was done to

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: her.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Sir, your honour cannot come to that yet.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: No, sir, nor I mean it not.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Sir, but you shall come to it, by your honour’s leave. And I beseech

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: you, look into Master Froth here, sir, a man of fourscore pound a year;

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: whose father died at Hallowmas—was’t not at Hallowmas, Master Froth?

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: All-hallond Eve.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Why, very well. I hope here be truths. He, sir, sitting, as I say, in a

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: lower chair, sir—’twas in the Bunch of Grapes, where, indeed, you have

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: a delight to sit, have you not?

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: I have so, because it is an open room, and good for winter.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Why, very well then. I hope here be truths.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: This will last out a night in Russia

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: When nights are longest there. I’ll take my leave,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And leave you to the hearing of the cause;

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Hoping you’ll find good cause to whip them all.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: I think no less. Good morrow to your lordship.
[_Exit Angelo._]

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Now, sir, come on. What was done to Elbow’s wife, once more?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Once, sir? There was nothing done to her once.

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: I beseech you, sir, ask him what this man did to my wife.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: I beseech your honour, ask me.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Well, sir, what did this gentleman to her?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: I beseech you, sir, look in this gentleman’s face. Good Master Froth,

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: look upon his honour; ’tis for a good purpose.—Doth your honour mark

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: his face?

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Ay, sir, very well.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Nay, I beseech you, mark it well.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Well, I do so.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Doth your honour see any harm in his face?

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Why, no.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: I’ll be supposed upon a book, his face is the worst thing about him.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Good, then, if his face be the worst thing about him, how could Master

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Froth do the constable’s wife any harm? I would know that of your

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: honour.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: He’s in the right. Constable. What say you to it?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: First, an it like you, the house is a respected house; next, this is a

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: respected fellow; and his mistress is a respected woman.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: By this hand, sir, his wife is a more respected person than any of us

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: all.

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Varlet, thou liest; thou liest, wicked varlet! The time is yet to come

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: that she was ever respected with man, woman, or child.

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Sir, she was respected with him before he married with her.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Which is the wiser here, Justice or Iniquity? Is this true?

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: O thou caitiff! O thou varlet! O thou wicked Hannibal! I respected with

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: her before I was married to her? If ever I was respected with her, or

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: she with me, let not your worship think me the poor Duke’s officer.

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Prove this, thou wicked Hannibal, or I’ll have mine action of battery

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: on thee.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: If he took you a box o’ th’ ear, you might have your action of slander

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: too.

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Marry, I thank your good worship for it. What is’t your worship’s

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: pleasure I shall do with this wicked caitiff?

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Truly, officer, because he hath some offences in him that thou wouldst

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: discover if thou couldst, let him continue in his courses till thou

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: know’st what they are.

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: Marry, I thank your worship for it.—Thou seest, thou wicked varlet,

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: now, what’s come upon thee. Thou art to continue now, thou varlet, thou

lines.speaker: ELBOW
lines.text: art to continue.
[_To Froth_.]

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Where were you born, friend?

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: Here in Vienna, sir.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Are you of fourscore pounds a year?

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: Yes, an’t please you, sir.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: So. [_To Pompey_.] What trade are you of, sir?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: A tapster, a poor widow’s tapster.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Your mistress’ name?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Mistress Overdone.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Hath she had any more than one husband?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Nine, sir; Overdone by the last.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Nine?—Come hither to me, Master Froth. Master Froth, I would not have

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: you acquainted with tapsters; they will draw you, Master Froth, and you

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: will hang them. Get you gone, and let me hear no more of you.

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: I thank your worship. For mine own part, I never come into any room in

lines.speaker: FROTH
lines.text: a taphouse but I am drawn in.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Well, no more of it, Master Froth. Farewell.
[_Exit Froth._]

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: Come you hither to me, Master tapster. What’s your name, Master

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: tapster?

lines.speaker: POMPEY
lines.text: Pompey.

lines.speaker: ESCALUS
lines.text: What else?

lines.speaker: POMPEY

lines.text: As I do think, tomorrow.
[_To Juliet_.]

lines.speaker: PROVOST
lines.text: I have provided for you; stay a while

lines.speaker: PROVOST
lines.text: And you shall be conducted.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Repent you, fair one, of the sin you carry?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I do; and bear the shame most patiently.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I’ll teach you how you shall arraign your conscience,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And try your penitence, if it be sound

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Or hollowly put on.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I’ll gladly learn.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Love you the man that wronged you?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Yes, as I love the woman that wronged him.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: So then it seems your most offenceful act

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Was mutually committed?

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Mutually.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Then was your sin of heavier kind than his.

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I do confess it, and repent it, father.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: ’Tis meet so, daughter; but lest you do repent

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: As that the sin hath brought you to this shame,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Which sorrow is always toward ourselves, not heaven,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Showing we would not spare heaven as we love it,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But as we stand in fear—

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: I do repent me as it is an evil,

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: And take the shame with joy.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: There rest.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Your partner, as I hear, must die tomorrow,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And I am going with instruction to him.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Grace go with you! _Benedicite!_
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Must die tomorrow? O, injurious love

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: That respites me a life, whose very comfort

lines.speaker: JULIET
lines.text: Is still a dying horror!

lines.speaker: PROVOST
lines.text: ’Tis pity of him.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Angelo.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: When I would pray and think, I think and pray

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To several subjects. Heaven hath my empty words,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Whilst my invention, hearing not my tongue,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Anchors on Isabel. Heaven in my mouth,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: As if I did but only chew his name,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And in my heart the strong and swelling evil

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Of my conception. The state whereon I studied

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Is, like a good thing being often read,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Grown sere and tedious; yea, my gravity,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Wherein—let no man hear me—I take pride,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Could I with boot change for an idle plume

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Which the air beats for vain. O place, O form,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: How often dost thou with thy case, thy habit,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Wrench awe from fools, and tie the wiser souls

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To thy false seeming! Blood, thou art blood.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Let’s write good angel on the devil’s horn.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: ’Tis not the devil’s crest.
[_Knock within._]

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: How now, who’s there?
Enter Servant.

lines.speaker: SERVANT
lines.text: One Isabel, a sister, desires access to you.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Teach her the way.
[_Exit Servant._]

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: O heavens,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Why does my blood thus muster to my heart,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Making both it unable for itself

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And dispossessing all my other parts

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Of necessary fitness?

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: So play the foolish throngs with one that swoons,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Come all to help him, and so stop the air

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: By which he should revive. And even so

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: The general subject to a well-wished king

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Quit their own part, and in obsequious fondness

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Crowd to his presence, where their untaught love

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Must needs appear offence.
Enter Isabella.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: How now, fair maid?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I am come to know your pleasure.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That you might know it, would much better please me

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Than to demand what ’tis. Your brother cannot live.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Even so. Heaven keep your honour.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Yet may he live a while. And, it may be,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: As long as you or I. Yet he must die.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Under your sentence?

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Yea.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: When, I beseech you? That in his reprieve,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Longer or shorter, he may be so fitted

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: That his soul sicken not.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Ha! Fie, these filthy vices! It were as good

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To pardon him that hath from nature stolen

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: A man already made, as to remit

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Their saucy sweetness that do coin heaven’s image

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: In stamps that are forbid. ’Tis all as easy

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Falsely to take away a life true made

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: As to put metal in restrained means

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To make a false one.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: ’Tis set down so in heaven, but not in earth.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Say you so? Then I shall pose you quickly.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Which had you rather, that the most just law

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Now took your brother’s life; or, to redeem him,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Give up your body to such sweet uncleanness

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: As she that he hath stained?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Sir, believe this:

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I had rather give my body than my soul.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I talk not of your soul. Our compelled sins

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Stand more for number than for accompt.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: How say you?

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Nay, I’ll not warrant that, for I can speak

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Against the thing I say. Answer to this:

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I, now the voice of the recorded law,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Pronounce a sentence on your brother’s life.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Might there not be a charity in sin

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To save this brother’s life?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Please you to do’t,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I’ll take it as a peril to my soul;

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: It is no sin at all, but charity.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Pleased you to do’t at peril of your soul,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Were equal poise of sin and charity.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: That I do beg his life, if it be sin,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Heaven let me bear it. You granting of my suit,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: If that be sin, I’ll make it my morn prayer

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To have it added to the faults of mine,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And nothing of your answer.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Nay, but hear me.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Your sense pursues not mine. Either you are ignorant,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Or seem so, crafty; and that’s not good.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Let me be ignorant, and in nothing good,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: But graciously to know I am no better.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Thus wisdom wishes to appear most bright

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: When it doth tax itself, as these black masks

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Proclaim an enshield beauty ten times louder

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Than beauty could, displayed. But mark me;

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To be received plain, I’ll speak more gross.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Your brother is to die.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: So.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And his offence is so, as it appears,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Accountant to the law upon that pain.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: True.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Admit no other way to save his life—

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: As I subscribe not that, nor any other,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: But, in the loss of question, that you, his sister,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Finding yourself desired of such a person

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Whose credit with the judge, or own great place,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Could fetch your brother from the manacles

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Of the all-binding law; and that there were

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: No earthly mean to save him but that either

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: You must lay down the treasures of your body

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To this supposed, or else to let him suffer,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: What would you do?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: As much for my poor brother as myself.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: That is, were I under the terms of death,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Th’ impression of keen whips I’d wear as rubies,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And strip myself to death as to a bed

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: That longing have been sick for, ere I’d yield

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: My body up to shame.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Then must your brother die.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And ’twere the cheaper way.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Better it were a brother died at once

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Than that a sister, by redeeming him,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Should die for ever.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Were not you then as cruel as the sentence

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That you have slandered so?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Ignominy in ransom and free pardon

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Are of two houses. Lawful mercy

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Is nothing kin to foul redemption.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: You seemed of late to make the law a tyrant,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And rather proved the sliding of your brother

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: A merriment than a vice.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: O, pardon me, my lord. It oft falls out,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To have what we would have, we speak not what we mean.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I something do excuse the thing I hate

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: For his advantage that I dearly love.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: We are all frail.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Else let my brother die,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: If not a feodary but only he

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Owe and succeed by weakness.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Nay, women are frail too.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Ay, as the glasses where they view themselves,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Which are as easy broke as they make forms.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Women?—Help, heaven! Men their creation mar

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: In profiting by them. Nay, call us ten times frail;

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: For we are soft as our complexions are,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And credulous to false prints.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I think it well.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And from this testimony of your own sex,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Since I suppose we are made to be no stronger

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Than faults may shake our frames, let me be bold.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I do arrest your words. Be that you are,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That is, a woman. If you be more, you’re none.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: If you be one, as you are well expressed

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: By all external warrants, show it now

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: By putting on the destined livery.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I have no tongue but one. Gentle my lord,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Let me intreat you speak the former language.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Plainly conceive, I love you.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: My brother did love Juliet,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And you tell me that he shall die for ’t.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: He shall not, Isabel, if you give me love.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I know your virtue hath a license in’t,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Which seems a little fouler than it is,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To pluck on others.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Believe me, on mine honour,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: My words express my purpose.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Ha! Little honour to be much believed,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And most pernicious purpose! Seeming, seeming!

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I will proclaim thee, Angelo, look for’t.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Sign me a present pardon for my brother

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Or with an outstretched throat I’ll tell the world aloud

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: What man thou art.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Who will believe thee, Isabel?

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: My unsoiled name, th’ austereness of my life,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: My vouch against you, and my place i’ th’ state

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Will so your accusation overweigh

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That you shall stifle in your own report,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And smell of calumny. I have begun,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And now I give my sensual race the rein.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Fit thy consent to my sharp appetite;

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Lay by all nicety and prolixious blushes

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That banish what they sue for. Redeem thy brother

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: By yielding up thy body to my will;

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Or else he must not only die the death,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: But thy unkindness shall his death draw out

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To ling’ring sufferance. Answer me tomorrow,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Or, by the affection that now guides me most,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I’ll prove a tyrant to him. As for you,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Say what you can, my false o’erweighs your true.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To whom should I complain? Did I tell this,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Who would believe me? O perilous mouths,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: That bear in them one and the self-same tongue

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Either of condemnation or approof,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Bidding the law make curtsy to their will,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Hooking both right and wrong to th’ appetite,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To follow as it draws! I’ll to my brother.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Though he hath fall’n by prompture of the blood,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Yet hath he in him such a mind of honour

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: That, had he twenty heads to tender down

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: On twenty bloody blocks, he’d yield them up

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Before his sister should her body stoop

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To such abhorred pollution.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Then, Isabel, live chaste, and, brother, die.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: More than our brother is our chastity.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: I’ll tell him yet of Angelo’s request,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: And fit his mind to death, for his soul’s rest.
[_Exit._]
Enter Duke, Claudio and Provost.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: So then you hope of pardon from Lord Angelo?

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: The miserable have no other medicine

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But only hope.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I have hope to live, and am prepared to die.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Be absolute for death. Either death or life

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Shall thereby be the sweeter. Reason thus with life:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: If I do lose thee, I do lose a thing

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That none but fools would keep. A breath thou art,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Servile to all the skyey influences

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That dost this habitation where thou keep’st

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Hourly afflict. Merely, thou art death’s fool;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For him thou labour’st by thy flight to shun,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And yet runn’st toward him still. Thou art not noble;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For all th’ accommodations that thou bear’st

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Are nursed by baseness. Thou’rt by no means valiant;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For thou dost fear the soft and tender fork

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Of a poor worm. Thy best of rest is sleep,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And that thou oft provok’st, yet grossly fear’st

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thy death, which is no more. Thou art not thyself;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For thou exists on many a thousand grains

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That issue out of dust. Happy thou art not;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For what thou hast not, still thou striv’st to get,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And what thou hast, forget’st. Thou art not certain;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For thy complexion shifts to strange effects

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: After the moon. If thou art rich, thou’rt poor;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For, like an ass whose back with ingots bows,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thou bear’st thy heavy riches but a journey,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And death unloads thee. Friend hast thou none;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For thine own bowels which do call thee sire,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The mere effusion of thy proper loins,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Do curse the gout, serpigo, and the rheum

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For ending thee no sooner. Thou hast nor youth nor age,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But as it were an after-dinner’s sleep

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Dreaming on both; for all thy blessed youth

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Becomes as aged, and doth beg the alms

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Of palsied eld; and when thou art old and rich,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thou hast neither heat, affection, limb, nor beauty

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To make thy riches pleasant. What’s yet in this

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That bears the name of life? Yet in this life

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Lie hid more thousand deaths; yet death we fear,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: That makes these odds all even.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: I humbly thank you.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: To sue to live, I find I seek to die,

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: And seeking death, find life. Let it come on.
[_Within_.]

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: What ho! Peace here; grace and good company!

lines.speaker: PROVOST
lines.text: Who’s there? Come in. The wish deserves a welcome.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Dear sir, ere long I’ll visit you again.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Most holy sir, I thank you.
Enter Isabella.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: My business is a word or two with Claudio.

lines.speaker: PROVOST
lines.text: And very welcome. Look, signior, here’s your sister.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Provost, a word with you.

lines.speaker: PROVOST
lines.text: As many as you please.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Bring me to hear them speak, where I may be concealed.
[_Exeunt Duke and Provost._]

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Now, sister, what’s the comfort?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Why,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: As all comforts are, most good, most good indeed.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Lord Angelo, having affairs to heaven,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Intends you for his swift ambassador,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Where you shall be an everlasting leiger.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Therefore your best appointment make with speed;

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Tomorrow you set on.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Is there no remedy?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: None, but such remedy as, to save a head,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: To cleave a heart in twain.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: But is there any?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Yes, brother, you may live.

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: There is a devilish mercy in the judge,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: If you’ll implore it, that will free your life,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: But fetter you till death.

lines.speaker: CLAUDIO
lines.text: Perpetual durance?

lines.speaker: ISABELLA
lines.text: Ay, just; perpetual durance; a restraint,

lines.speaker: ISABELLA

lines.text: To a determined scope.
